elements.element: Customer is not subject to any exclusivity obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 prohibits the Company from participating in similar Internet projects involving Deerskin Products and grants HDI an exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand for the specified website.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not require the Company to purchase products or services solely from HDI.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restriction is confined to the capitalized category “Deerskin Products”; the original references to products “substantially similar” to Deerskin Products and similar companies have been removed.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only “during the period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date,” notwithstanding the Agreement's potential renewal.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet any service level.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the restrictions on the Company terminate automatically upon any failure by HDI to meet any service level under the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity obligations terminate automatically if Vendor fails to meet any delivery date.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the restrictions on the Company terminate automatically upon any failure by HDI to meet any delivery date under the Agreement.

result.reason: The redline retains Customer exclusivity, so it does not satisfy the preferred position. It satisfies the fallback by narrowing the covered products to Deerskin Products, limiting the restriction to 12 months, and providing automatic release upon any HDI service-level or delivery-date failure. The changes are limited to those needed for the fallback and leave unrelated termination terms intact. Drafting quality is reduced because “exclusive right to use of” is grammatically awkward and the release of HDI's exclusive right could be stated more directly rather than referring generally to “restrictions on the Company.”
